newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Erbakan rules out early elections.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Erbakan rules out early elections.

text.p: Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan on Saturday ruled out early elections as a solution to his dispute with the secularist army over Islamist activism, Anatolian news agency said.
"Going to elections would mean coming under the influence of a false agenda," the agency quoted him as telling a meeting of local heads of his Welfare Party.

Erbakan last weekend threatened the divided opposition with snap polls in what was seen as a tactical move. The other parties have not taken up his challenge to ask the voters to mediate his row with the generals.
The secularist army has put Erbakan, modern Turkey's first Islamist prime minister, under heavy pressure to crack down on a Moslem religious upsurge.
Erbakan's wing of the coalition government has stalled in taking anti-Islamist action.
The interior minister, from the ruling alliance's secularist faction, on Saturday vowed to close down thousands of outlawed Islamic education centres.
